meta.title: FAQ
meta.description: Answers about Capstio: which macOS and Linux versions it supports, whether it installs anything on your VPS, when alerts run, where AI requests go and where your SSH keys live.

title: Frequently asked questions
intro: The questions people ask most about Capstio, grouped by topic. The answers only cover what the app does today.

items.question: Which macOS versions and Macs does Capstio run on?
items.answer: macOS 15 or later, with Apple Silicon Macs first. Capstio is a native Mac app written in Swift and SwiftUI.

items.question: Is there a Windows or Linux version?
items.answer: No. Capstio is a Mac app. It runs on your Mac and connects to your Linux servers over SSH.

items.question: Can I keep my existing hosts and SSH keys?
items.answer: Yes. The first-run screen imports the hosts you already have in ~/.ssh/config, and you keep using your current SSH keys. Capstio can also create or import Ed25519 and RSA keys.

items.question: Which kinds of apps does Capstio find on a server?
items.answer: Apps run by Docker Compose, PM2 and systemd, in one list. Each app keeps its processes, config, logs and status in one place, however it was started.

items.question: What does the server need?
items.answer: Just SSH. Capstio installs no agent on your VPS. Some features use Docker, PM2 or systemd already on the server; on distributions with limited support, features that do not apply are hidden.

items.question: Is editing config on the server safe?
items.answer: The editor checks syntax as you type, and every save makes a backup on the server first. You can review the diff and restore an earlier version in one click.

items.question: Do alerts work when Capstio is closed?
items.answer: No. Alerts run only while Capstio is open on your Mac. They appear as macOS notifications and can also go to Slack or a webhook.

items.question: What can Capstio alert me about?
items.answer: Disk, CPU or RAM over a threshold, containers that keep restarting, a host losing its connection, SSL certificates about to expire, pending security updates and suspicious SSH logins. You can set your own thresholds.

items.question: Which AI providers can I use?
items.answer: Anthropic and OpenAI with your own API key, Claude Code and Codex with your own account, or Ollama running on your Mac. AI only works once you turn it on.

items.question: Where do AI requests go?
items.answer: Straight from your Mac to the provider you pick, never through Capstio servers. Secrets are masked before anything is sent; if you want to be certain, use a local model through Ollama.

items.question: Can the AI run commands on my server by itself?
items.answer: No. The AI suggests read-only commands and you approve each one. Capstio, not the model, decides which commands count as read-only.

items.question: Does the app collect usage data?
items.answer: The app embeds no analytics or tracking SDK. Your terminal, logs, metrics and file contents are never sent to Capstio servers.

items.question: What can the team vault server see?
items.answer: Shared hosts, SSH keys and recipes are end-to-end encrypted, and the server only stores ciphertext. Metadata such as the number of hosts and who changed what, and when, stays readable.

items.question: Can team data be recovered if I lose my devices?
items.answer: You hold a recovery key for that. If you lose every device and the recovery key as well, the team data cannot be recovered.

items.question: How do I sign in?
items.answer: With Google or a code sent by email, and only when you need teamwork or sync. Sign in with Apple is not available.
